summary.title: Summary
summary.text: Software engineer who cares about polished, thoughtful UI — the details, the edge cases, how an interface behaves in a real user's hands — and about the engineering underneath it: reusable cores instead of copy-paste, architecture that keeps the UI responsive, backward compatibility as a deliberate decision, tests in every significant change. Currently working in the core of a complex interactive editor used by millions. Also built the i18n infrastructure for ten languages and treat it as an engineering problem rather than translation: typed pipelines and CI gates. Used to working as a self-directed engineer in an async product team — taking things from a fuzzy idea to production and steady state.

experience.title: Experience
experience.note: Listed here are only the projects I still run today — there have been others along the way. Outside of client work I also build systems and modules for FoundryVTT (so far for my own tabletop campaigns and friends) and localize tabletop rulebooks, games and guides from English to Russian, communicating with their authors in English along the way.

jobs.description: Popular guitar tablature service with a multi-million user audience. I work on the core of the product's interactive editor — features that touch domain rules, the data model and rendering, not just screens — plus product experiments and the frontend i18n platform, in an async remote team.
bullets: Shipped a notation feature end-to-end across three repositories — file-import parsing in a separately versioned package, data model, editor UI, user docs and ten languages — with a deliberate backward-compatibility design so existing user content kept behaving exactly as before.

Designed a reusable core for a family of editor commands that move notes under real instrument constraints, and rebuilt three commands on top of it; the same logic drives both the command and the toolbar state, so controls are disabled exactly where the action would fail.

Built an interaction layer over an SVG-rendered document: clickable notation symbols that open the right editing tools (12 components, each with a component test), geometry-based mapping between symbols and data, and a hover preview showing what a toolbar command will affect.

Architected a read-only command preview computed in a Web Worker: runs against a throwaway copy of the document, renders through the production pipeline, defers expensive work so a user's click never waits behind a hover preview, and drops stale responses — in review.

Unified the app's floating UI — dropdowns, pickers, settings panels — behind a single shared hook, removing per-component boilerplate; redesigned complex notation UI with a responsive mobile layout and contextual help.

Built and maintain the i18n platform: ten languages across hundreds of components on a typed gettext/.po workflow with grammar-aware word order, plus a static analyzer with auto-fix and translation-quality tests wired into the CI of three services — turning a class of localization bugs from manual QA into automated gates.

Run product A/B experiments end-to-end — experiment design and exposure rules, UI, analytics attribution, e2e coverage and QA coordination — including source attribution for the subscription upgrade funnel.
